home.welcomeMessage: Use the navigation above to manage routes and extract timetables from Train Sim World.
home.gettingStartedDesc: Learn how to use the TSW HUD PROJECT to track your train journeys.
home.instruction1Intro: Use OCR to automatically extract timetable data from Train Sim World screenshots.
home.instruction2Intro: Build a timetable from scratch by entering each stop manually.
home.instruction3Intro: Import previously exported timetables or share timetables with others.
home.instruction4Intro: Record GPS coordinates for your timetable by running the route in Train Sim World while connected to the HUD Project.
home.instruction5Intro: Automatically record coordinates for your timetable entries while the AI drives the route for you. This explanation sounds more complicated than it is - a video tutorial will be added soon.
home.instruction6Intro: View your live train position on the map while playing Train Sim World.

instructions.captureScreenshotsDesc: In Train Sim World, open your timetable and take screenshots of:
instructions.timetableHeader: The timetable header showing the service name and times
instructions.timetableEntries: The detailed timetable entries showing stops, platforms, and times
instructions.uploadImagesStep2: In the "Extract from Images" section, click or drag your screenshots into the upload area
instructions.uploadImagesStep3: The system will automatically process the images using OCR
instructions.reviewDataStep1: Review the extracted timetable entries in the table
instructions.reviewDataStep2: Click on any cell to edit if the OCR made mistakes
instructions.reviewDataStep3: Ensure the Action type is correctly selected for each row
instructions.reviewDataStep4: Check that times are in HH:MM:SS format (e.g., 16:13:00)
instructions.completeTimetableStep1: Enter or verify the Service Name
instructions.completeTimetableStep2: Select a Route from the dropdown
instructions.completeTimetableStep3: Select at least one Formation for this service
instructions.importantFirstLocation: The first location and first platform are not included in the in-game timetable screenshots and will need to be added manually.
instructions.startNewTimetableStep2: Click the "+ Create New Timetable" button
instructions.enterBasicInfoStep1: Enter the Service Name (e.g., "1C84 London Paddington to Penzance")
instructions.enterBasicInfoStep2: Select the Route from the dropdown
instructions.enterBasicInfoStep3: Select one or more Formations that can run this service
instructions.addEntriesDesc: Click "+ Add Entry" to add stops. For each entry:
instructions.addEntriesAction: Action: Select the type (WAIT FOR SERVICE, STOP AT LOCATION, LOAD PASSENGERS, etc.)
instructions.addEntriesPlatform: Platform: Enter the platform number if applicable
instructions.addEntriesQuickAdd: Use the "Quick Add Common Entries" buttons to quickly add preset actions.
instructions.saveTimetableDesc: Click "Create Timetable" when all entries are added.
instructions.tipEditLater: You can always edit the timetable later by clicking on it in the timetables list.
instructions.importingStep2: In the "Import Timetable" section, click or drag a JSON file into the upload area
instructions.importingStep3: The system will validate and import the timetable automatically
instructions.importingStep4: You'll be redirected to the timetable view on success
instructions.exportingStep1: Open any timetable from the list
instructions.exportingStep3: Save the JSON file to share or backup
instructions.tipJsonExport: JSON exports include all timetable data including coordinates, making them perfect for backups or sharing complete routes.
instructions.openRecordMapStep1: Go to the Record Map page
instructions.openRecordMapStep2: Select your Route from the dropdown
instructions.openRecordMapStep5: Select the Timetable you want to record
instructions.startRecordingStep1: Start Train Sim World and load your service
instructions.startRecordingStep2: Click the "Start" button on the Record Map page
instructions.startRecordingStep3: Begin driving your route - coordinates will be recorded automatically
instructions.startRecordingStep4: The map will show your path in real-time
instructions.saveStationPositionsDesc: As you arrive at each station:
instructions.saveStationPositionsStep1: Select the station from the "Select Station" dropdown
instructions.saveStationPositionsStep2: Click "Save Position" to record the coordinates
instructions.saveStationPositionsStep3: The station will be marked with a green marker on the map
instructions.completeRecordingStep1: When finished, click "Save" to process and save all data
instructions.completeRecordingStep2: The recording will be processed and saved to the database
instructions.completeRecordingStep3: Click "Reset" to clear and start fresh if needed
instructions.automaticDesc: Recording auto-stops after 2 minutes of no movement
instructions.manualDesc: Recording continues until you click Save
instructions.tipPause: Use the "Pause" button if you need to take a break during recording. Resume when ready to continue.
instructions.inGameSetupStep4: Take a screenshot of the service name
instructions.inGameSetupStep6: Do not touch any train controls
instructions.inGameSetupStep8: Take screenshots of the schedule (multiple if needed)
instructions.inTheAppStep4: Upload your screenshots to the Timetables page
instructions.importantScreenshotOrder: The order of screenshots matters! They need to be in chronological order. If your screenshots have timestamps and you followed the flow above, you will be fine.
instructions.completeTimetableDataStep1: Go to Route Map to get the first location name and platform number
instructions.completeTimetableDataStep2: Add the location name and platform number to the timetable
instructions.completeTimetableDataStep3: Review and confirm the data - the "Service Name" often has OCR errors, but timetable data is usually accurate
instructions.startAutoRecordingStep2: Select your route, formation, and timetable
instructions.enableAIDriverStep1: Use God Mode to access the console commands
instructions.enableAIDriverStep2: Enable the "Relinquish Service" command from the God Mode menu
instructions.enableAIDriverStep4: Come back when automatic recording is complete
instructions.loadTimetableStep1: Go to the Tracking Map page
instructions.loadTimetableStep2: In the "Load Timetable" section, select your Route
instructions.loadTimetableStep4: Select a Timetable (only timetables with recorded coordinates will appear)
instructions.viewLiveTrackingDesc: Once connected to Train Sim World:
instructions.viewLiveTrackingOrange: Your train position appears as an orange marker
instructions.viewLiveTrackingBlue: The route path is shown as a blue line
instructions.viewLiveTrackingGreen: Station stops are marked with green circles
instructions.viewLiveTrackingInfo: The info panel shows your current speed and direction
instructions.timetableInfoNextStop: Next Stop Time: Scheduled time for the next station
instructions.timetableInfoDistance: Distance: Distance remaining to the next stop
instructions.followModeStep1: Click "Follow Train" to keep the map centered on your position
instructions.followModeStep2: Click "Stop Following" to browse the map freely
instructions.tipOpenHUD: Click "Open HUD" to open a dedicated heads-up display window that you can position alongside your game.
instructions.stopDetectionDesc1: Each stop (including the first) must be recorded stopped for a minimum of 30 seconds to be identified as a stop
instructions.stopDetectionDesc2: If the train doesn't move for around 5 minutes (usually at the last stop), the server will automatically stop recording, identify all stops based on timing, and save everything to the database
instructions.benefitDesc: This method lets you enjoy all the data that comes from a full route recording without having to sit through the entire journey!
instructions.ocrIntro: Use OCR to automatically extract timetable data from Train Sim World screenshots. You need to capture 8 or more images in a specific order.
instructions.ocrCaptureDesc: In Train Sim World, capture these screenshots in order. Name them so they sort alphabetically (e.g., 1.png, 2.png, ... or use any names that sort correctly).
instructions.ocrImage1Desc: The route name from the service selection screen.
instructions.ocrImage2Desc: The service header showing the full service name, start time, and duration.
instructions.ocrImage5Desc: The train tonnage value from the level info bar.
instructions.ocrImage6Desc: The number of cars in the consist.
instructions.ocrImage7Desc: The train length in meters from the level info bar.
instructions.ocrImage8Desc: Screenshot each page of the timetable showing the stops, actions, and times. Capture as many pages as needed to cover the full timetable.
instructions.ocrImage8Caption1: Example: Timetable page 1 - WAIT FOR SERVICE, stops, and times
instructions.ocrImage8Caption2: Example: Timetable page 2 - continuation of stops
instructions.ocrUploadStep1: Go to the Timetables page or a Formation detail page
instructions.ocrUploadStep2: In the "Extract from Images" section, click or drag your screenshots into the upload area
instructions.ocrUploadStep3: Make sure files are named so they sort in the correct order (1.png, 2.png, ... or alphabetically)
instructions.ocrUploadStep4: The system will automatically process the images using OCR
instructions.ocrReviewStep1: The route will be auto-matched and locations will populate as dropdowns
instructions.ocrReviewStep2: Start time, duration, tonnage, car count, and train length will appear in the Level Info bar
instructions.ocrReviewStep3: Review the extracted timetable entries in the table
instructions.ocrReviewStep4: Click on any cell to edit if the OCR made mistakes
instructions.ocrReviewStep5: Check that times are in HH:MM:SS format (e.g., 14:28:00)
instructions.ocrCompleteStep1: Enter or verify the Service Name
instructions.ocrCompleteStep2: Confirm the Route was correctly matched (or select one manually)
instructions.ocrCompleteStep3: Select at least one Formation for this service
instructions.ocrImportantNote: The first location and first platform are not included in the in-game timetable screenshots and will need to be added manually.
instructions.newMethodIntro: Automatically capture all service data for a route using AI-powered screen reading. This bot uses the Claude API to navigate Train Sim World menus and extract timetable data without manual screenshots.
instructions.newMethodPrereq1: Anthropic API key set as environment variable (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)
instructions.newMethodPrereq3: Train Sim World installed and configured
instructions.newMethodPhase1Desc: Launches TSW, navigates to the route selection screen, and selects the configured route
instructions.newMethodPhase2Desc: Scrolls through all service pages and captures screenshots of each one
instructions.newMethodPhase3Desc: Uses Claude API to analyze captured pages and identify all service names and positions
instructions.newMethodPhase4Desc: Clicks each service, captures the timetable data, and uploads it to the HUD database
instructions.newMethodCmd1: Full run: launches game, captures all services
instructions.newMethodCmd2: Skip game launch (game already running and on service screen)
instructions.newMethodCmd3: Resume from a specific formation, formation number, and service number
instructions.newMethodConfigurationDesc: Before running, update ROUTE_NAME in bot/config.py to match your target route. Progress is saved automatically to progress_new_method.json, so the bot can resume if interrupted.
instructions.newMethodWarning: Do not move the mouse or interact with the computer while the bot is running. It controls the mouse and keyboard to navigate game menus.
instructions.newMethodTip: Use --no-launch when the game is already open to save time. The bot will start from the service selection screen.
instructions.calibrateIntro: Calibrate the bot's screen coordinates for your display resolution. This interactive 21-step tool captures reference images and measures pixel positions for all UI elements the bot needs to click.
instructions.calibrateWhen1: First time setting up the bot on a new computer
instructions.calibrateWhen2: After changing your display resolution or scaling
instructions.calibrateWhen3: After a Train Sim World update that changes the UI layout
instructions.calibrateWhen4: If the bot is clicking in wrong positions
instructions.calibrateStepsDesc: The tool guides you through capturing each game screen. Here are some of the key reference images it captures:
instructions.calibrateOutput2: Generated Python config with calibrated values
instructions.calibrateOutput3: Updated reference images for screen matching
instructions.calibrateTip: If only specific elements are misaligned, use --step N to recalibrate just that step instead of running the full calibration.
instructions.serviceScrollIntro: Test and fine-tune the click positions for each service in the service list. This tool verifies that the bot can correctly click on every service entry, and helps you adjust Y-position drift per page.
instructions.serviceScrollPrereq1: A services.csv file generated from a previous calibration or bot run
instructions.serviceScrollPrereq2: Train Sim World running and on the service selection screen
instructions.serviceScrollCmd1: Test all services from the beginning
instructions.serviceScrollCmd4: Reset and start from the beginning
instructions.serviceScrollHow1: The tool scrolls to each service's page in the game
instructions.serviceScrollHow2: It clicks the service at the calculated Y-position
instructions.serviceScrollHow3: It captures a screenshot and uses AI to verify the correct service was selected
instructions.serviceScrollHow4: If wrong, use the global hotkeys to nudge the Y-position up or down
instructions.serviceScrollHow5: At the end, it outputs suggested PAGE_Y_DRIFT values for config.py
instructions.serviceScrollDriftDesc: Different pages in the service list may have slight vertical offsets. The tool detects these and suggests per-page drift corrections that you add to PAGE_Y_DRIFT in bot/config.py. You can also run python evaluate_drift.py to automatically compare captured data against expected values.
instructions.serviceScrollTip: During testing, use the global hotkeys to adjust click positions in real-time. The adjustments are saved and reported at the end as drift suggestions.

recordingSettings.title: Recording Settings
recordingSettings.subtitle: Configure recording behavior and route processing parameters
recordingSettings.simplifyToleranceDesc: Points within this distance of the simplified line are removed. Lower values preserve more detail but create larger files. Default: 1
recordingSettings.minStopDurationDesc: How long the train must be stationary to count as a stop during automatic recording. Default: 30
recordingSettings.gpsNoiseRadiusDesc: Maximum distance for coordinates to be considered the same location during stop detection. Default: 10
recordingSettings.minPointsForStopDesc: Minimum number of coordinate data points needed to form a valid stop cluster. Default: 10
recordingSettings.autoStopTimeoutDesc: In automatic mode, recording stops after this period of no movement once past the last timetable time. Default: 120
recordingSettings.saveFrequencyDesc: Save recording data to disk every N coordinates. 1 = every coordinate (safest). Higher values improve performance but risk data loss. Default: 1
recordingSettings.resetDesc: Reset all recording settings to their default values.

huds.experimentDesc: Minimal canvas-based HUD with a compact speedometer design. Used for testing new layouts and features before rolling out to other HUDs.
